- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit recent highs; use 3-period moving average or median of last 5 days as anchor.
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >5% gap), check if sentiment was high recently — if so, model may be overestimating sentiment-driven demand; reduce forecast by 1–4%.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after strong moves; apply 1–2% downward correction if price deviates >3σ from 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — increase forecast downward by 1–3% to reflect pessimism.
- Avoid forecasting above 76.5 unless sentiment is >0.8 and price is trending strongly upward — otherwise, cap at 76.0–76.5 to avoid overestimation.
